turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hey, Marcus here. You’ve got about twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Thanks, Marcus. Could I ask a few questions about why new AEs take seven months to ramp, then see whether a pilot makes sense?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Sure. What do you want to know?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Could you walk me through those seven months—what new AEs need to master, and where they typically stall?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: They need to understand the product and how it fits into a customer’s payments and reconciliation stack. They usually stall when integration questions get specific on live calls—they fumble the answers and lose credibility.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: How often do integration questions derail calls, and what does that lost credibility cost in delayed ramp or missed pipeline per AE?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Roughly a third of early calls hit an integration question the rep can’t handle. We don’t quantify the pipeline impact cleanly, but it creates extra technical follow-ups and contributes to that seven-month wait for a first close.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: When that happens on a third of early calls, how many follow-ups does engineering handle monthly, and how much time does each consume?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We don’t track it formally. I’d estimate 15 to 20 follow-ups a month, usually 30 to 60 minutes each depending on whether someone has to inspect the customer’s setup.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: So engineering loses roughly 8 to 20 hours monthly. Beyond that load, how are new AEs practicing integration conversations before live calls?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mostly they shadow experienced reps, read the integration docs, and role-play with a manager. The role-plays are fairly generic; they don’t reproduce the customer-specific edge cases that trip them up.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: How much manager time goes into those generic role-plays, and how do you decide an AE is ready for customer-specific integration questions?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I don’t know the exact manager time; Rachel would. Readiness is mostly subjective—finish onboarding, pass a few mock calls, then learn on live calls.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: If reps practiced customer-specific edge cases before live calls, what reduction in seven-month ramp and monthly follow-ups would make a change worthwhile?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: If it cut time to first close from seven months to five and halved those engineering follow-ups, that would be meaningful. How does your product actually make that happen?
